tests: [touchscreen.test] Touchscreen Touchscreen.prototype.touchMove should work with two touches
[touchscreen.test] Touchscreen Touchscreen.prototype.touchMove should work when moving touches separately
[touchscreen.test] Touchscreen Touchscreen.prototype.touchMove should work with three touches
[touchscreen.test] Touchscreen Touchscreen.prototype.touchMove should throw if no touch was started
[touchscreen.test] Touchscreen Touchscreen.prototype.touchEnd should throw when ending touch through Touchscreeen that was already ended
[touchscreen.test] Touchscreen Touchscreen.prototype.tap should work if another touch is already active
reason: Drives the touchscreen directly: `page.touchscreen.touchStart`, `touchMove`, and `touchEnd`, and the touch handles they return. Strider has no touchscreen; its only touch input is `Locator.tap`, which sends one tap and can't hold a touch down or move it
Taps the button, which needs touch input. Stock WebKit's automation builds without touch (`input.touch`), so `Locator.tap` fails with Unsupported before anything is sent
